mainTopic: Why שמואל needed all three statements; the year for tithing vegetables; and why the new year for trees falls in שבט
overview: First the גמרא explains why שמואל needed all three of his statements about tithing cowpeas: הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי, לכל אין בילה, and הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי. Each statement alone could be misunderstood, and another statement prevents that mistake. The last statement is limited to the beans in רבי שמעון שזורי's dispute, not grain and olives. The גמרא then asks why לכל אין בילה is needed at all. It answers that it teaches that wine and oil do blend. Next, a ברייתא brings רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא, who learn from the same פסוק which year vegetables are tithed for, each using a different test. רבי אבהו shows that their practical difference is seedless onions and cowpeas whose water was held back before ראש השנה. Finally the גמרא explains that the first of שבט is the new year for trees because most of the year's rain has fallen by then, even though most of the winter is still ahead. It then begins a story about רבי עקיבא's אתרוג that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the first statement alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens the צריכותא. If שמואל had only said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, we might think the reason is יש בילה (mixing blends everything). So he also said לכל אין בילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to say all of them. If שמואל had only taught that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, I would have said that this is because he holds mixing works. So he teaches us that for everything else there is no mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why שמואל needed all three statements. This step shows why the first statement (follow רבי שמעון שזורי) needs the second (לכל אין בילה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי allows the cowpeas of two years to be tithed together. A learner might guess his reason is that once everything is piled together it counts as one blended mass (בילה). שמואל's second statement, that solids never blend, rules that reason out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; the גמרא is explaining why each statement is needed
He taught us
I would have said; the mistaken first thought
Mixing that makes the pieces count as one blended mass
He teaches us; this is the point the extra statement adds

steps.confusionAlert: The הוה אמינא here is not a real opinion of שמואל. It is the mistake the גמרא says we would have made without the second statement.

phrases.english: And it is necessary: for if he had taught us only
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל. The גמרא is about to show why each of his three statements is needed.

phrases.english: that the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר יֵשׁ בִּילָּה,
phrases.english: I would have said: it is because he holds that there is mixing,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: for everything there is no mixing.
phrases.notes: This is short for שמואל's full statement that only liquids like wine and oil really blend.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the צריכותא for שמואל's three statements quoted earlier in the sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement 'הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי' alone could suggest a reason of יש בילה; the statement 'לכל אין בילה' is needed to rule that out.

steps.title: Why the second statement alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל had only said לכל אין בילה, we might think he agrees with the חכמים that the cowpeas cannot be tithed together. So he also said הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught that for everything there is no mixing, I would have said he holds like the חכמים. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes the other way: the second statement (לכל אין בילה) needs the first one (follow רבי שמעון שזורי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If solids do not blend, it would seem natural to agree with the חכמים, who say beans from two years cannot be tithed together. The first statement shows that שמואל still rules like רבי שמעון שזורי, so his reason must be something other than mixing.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים, who disagree with רבי שמעון שזורי here
He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only that for everything there is no mixing —
I would have said: he holds like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים who said the cowpeas from two different years may not be tithed together.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses step 1: now the second statement is shown to need the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לכל אין בילה' alone could suggest שמואל sides with the חכמים; 'הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי' is needed to show he does not.

steps.title: Why the third statement is needed to avoid a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: With only the first two statements, שמואל would seem to contradict himself: he follows רבי שמעון שזורי, whose reason might be mixing, yet he says solids never blend. The third statement, הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, gives the real reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught these two, I would have said that שמואל contradicts שמואל. So he teaches us that everything follows the full ripening of the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the first two statements together would look like a contradiction, and the third statement fixes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון שזורי's reason were בילה, then 'follow רבי שמעון שזורי' and 'solids do not blend' would clash. The third statement explains that his real reason is גמר פרי: all the beans finish ripening in one year, so they belong to one tithe year. Mixing has nothing to do with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (statements)
שמואל's statement contradicts שמואל's other statement
The full ripening of the produce

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real basis for following רבי שמעון שזורי: the tithe year is set by when the produce finishes ripening, not by mixing.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only these two —
I would have said: Shmuel's statement contradicts Shmuel's other statement,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר גְּמַר פֶּרִי.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: everything follows the full ripening of the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the first two statements and shows they would look contradictory without the third.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third statement, 'הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי', removes the apparent contradiction by giving the true reason behind רבי שמעון שזורי's view.

steps.title: Why the third statement alone is not enough: the limit to beans
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל had only said הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, we might apply it even to grain and olives. So he said הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי, which limits it to the case they disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught that everything follows the full ripening of the produce, I would have said that this applies even to grain and olives. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי only in the case where he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. It shows that the first statement is needed to keep the third from being applied too widely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכל' (everything) sounds like it covers all produce, including grain and olives. By tying the rule to רבי שמעון שזורי's specific dispute about the beans, שמואל limits it. Grain and olives keep their own rule: they follow the point when they reach one-third of their growth.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain
Olives
In the case where he disagrees

steps.whatToRemember: Each of שמואל's three statements protects against a mistake: 'follow רבי שמעון שזורי' is not because of בילה; 'אין בילה' does not mean he sides with the חכמים; 'גמר פרי' is the real reason, but it applies only to the beans in dispute, not to grain and olives.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי' to mean all produce. Grain and olives still follow one-third of their growth; the גמר פרי rule here covers only the beans of רבי שמעון שזורי's dispute.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר גְּמַר פֶּרִי —
phrases.english: And if he had taught us only that everything follows the full ripening of the produce —

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אֲפִילּוּ תְּבוּאָה וְזֵיתִים נָמֵי —
phrases.english: I would have said: even grain and olives as well —

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי
phrases.english: so he teaches us: the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri
in the case where he disagrees.
phrases.notes: That case is the beans. Grain and olives still go by when they reach one-third of their growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר גְּמַר פֶּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the third statement also needs the first, which limits its scope; this completes the צריכותא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three of שמואל's statements are needed. The rule of גמר פרי applies to the beans in רבי שמעון שזורי's dispute, while grain and olives follow one-third of their growth.

steps.title: Why do we need the statement that nothing blends?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: two of שמואל's statements seem to be enough, so why did he also say לכל אין בילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let שמואל just teach us these two statements. Why do I need "there is no mixing for anything"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether the statement לכל אין בילה is needed at all. It seems the other two statements already tell us everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the earlier steps, הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי plus הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי already gives us both the ruling and the reason. So the separate statement about mixing looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: "But let him teach us": a challenge that only some statements are needed
These two (statements)
Why do I need it? This asks why a statement is there at all.

phrases.english: But let him teach us these two,
phrases.notes: "These two" means הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי and הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי.

phrases.english: why do I need "there is no mixing for anything"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַשְׁמְעִינַן הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי, לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the צריכותא of steps 1–4, the גמרא asks whether one of the three statements is extra.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching does לכל אין בילה add beyond the other two statements?
steps.kashyaTarget: The צריכותא of steps 1–4, which claimed that לכל אין בילה is needed. With הלכה כרבי שמעון שזורי and הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, שמואל's position already seems complete.

steps.title: It teaches that wine and oil do blend
steps.stepSummary: The statement comes to teach that liquids like wine and oil do blend together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: for wine and oil there is mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the statement about mixing has its own lesson. It tells us that liquids are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לכל, "for all," means "for all solids." That wording quietly tells us that liquids like wine and oil do blend. So the statement is not extra. Its real lesson is about liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what it teaches us": the standard way to show the new point of a statement
Wine and oil, liquids that do mix together

steps.whatToRemember: Solids never blend (אין בילה), but liquids like wine and oil do blend (יש בילה).

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that for wine and oil there is mixing.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לכל אין בילה is needed to teach by implication that liquids such as wine and oil do blend.
steps.terutzMaskana: לכל אין בילה is not extra. Its point is the implied contrast that liquids such as wine and oil do blend.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: tithing follows which year's water the crop grows on
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the פסוק that crops growing on the old year's water are tithed for the old year. Vegetables grow on the new year's water, so they are tithed for the new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: "When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress." Grain and grapes grow on last year's water and are tithed for last year. So anything that grows on last year's water is tithed for last year. Vegetables are left out: they grow on the coming year's water, so they are tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי uses a פסוק to decide which year a crop counts for when it is tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain (גורן, threshing floor) and grapes (יקב, winepress) are the model. They grow on the water of the year before, so they are tithed for that year. Any crop like them follows the same rule. Vegetables grow on the new year's rain, so they belong to the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor and winepress, meaning grain and grapes/wine
The water of the year that has passed
They are tithed
Vegetables

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress";
just as the threshing floor and winepress are special
in that they grow on the water of the past year,
phrases.notes: He means the moisture left in the ground from last winter's rain.

phrases.english: and are tithed for the past year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל מֵי שָׁנָה שֶׁעָבְרָה
phrases.english: so too, anything that grows on the water of the past year
is tithed for the past year.
This leaves out vegetables,
which grow on the water of the coming year,
and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, a ברייתא about the tithing year of vegetables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crop is tithed for the year whose water it grew on. Vegetables grow on the new year's water, so they belong to the new year.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: tithing follows whether the crop lives on rain alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the same פסוק that crops that live mostly on rain are tithed for the old year. Vegetables need all kinds of water, including irrigation, so they are tithed for the new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: "When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress." Grain and grapes grow on most water and are tithed for last year. So anything that grows on most water is tithed for last year. Vegetables are left out: they grow on all water, so they are tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא reads the same פסוק in a different way. He uses a different test for which crops count for the old year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the test is not which year's water feeds the plant. The test is whether rain alone is enough (רוב מים) or the plant also needs to be watered by hand (כל מים). Vegetables need irrigation, so they go to the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: Most water, meaning rainfall is enough and no irrigation is needed
All water, meaning it also needs irrigation
The coming (new) year

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים quote the same פסוק and agree that vegetables go to the new year. They argue only about the reason, and that is why the גמרא next asks what difference it makes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress";
just as the threshing floor and winepress are special
in that they grow on most water,
phrases.notes: Rain is enough for them, so they don't need to be watered by hand.

phrases.english: and are tithed for the past year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל רוֹב מַיִם
phrases.english: so too, anything that grows on most water
is tithed for the past year.
This leaves out vegetables,
which grow on all water,
phrases.notes: He means they need irrigation too, not only rain.

phrases.english: and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק, with a different test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crop that lives mostly on rain is tithed for the old year. A crop that needs irrigation, like vegetables, is tithed for the new year.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two opinions would lead to a different result. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions put vegetables in the new year and grain and grapes in the old year. So the גמרא looks for a case where their different tests give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for the practical difference between two opinions.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא would rule differently.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: seedless onions and cowpeas
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the difference shows up with seedless onions and cowpeas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: seedless onions and cowpeas are the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו names the case where the two opinions split. The גמרא will next quote a משנה about that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These plants are grown as vegetables. If their water is held back, though, they stop growing on the new water. So under רבי יוסי הגלילי's test they could count for the old year. Under רבי עקיבא's test they are still plants that need irrigation.

keyTerms.meaning: Seedless onions, grown for their greens
Cowpea (literally "Egyptian bean")
There is (a difference) between them

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Seedless onions and cowpeas
are the difference between them.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute matters for seedless onions and cowpeas.

steps.title: The משנה about onions and cowpeas whose water was held back
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that seedless onions and cowpeas whose water was held back for thirty days before ראש השנה belong to the old year. Otherwise they belong to the new year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: seedless onions and cowpeas whose water was held back for thirty days before ראש השנה are tithed for the past year, and they are permitted in שביעית. If not, they are forbidden in שביעית and are tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that rules on רבי אבהו's case. This shows where the two opinions would split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה decides by what actually fed the plant. If its water was held back before ראש השנה, it counts for the old year. That matches רבי יוסי הגלילי's test of which year's water the plant grew on. רבי עקיבא would treat them as vegetables that need irrigation and put them in the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
That one held back water from them
The seventh year, the Sabbatical year
And if not

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי looks at which year's water the plant really grew on. רבי עקיבא looks at what kind of plant it is (rain-fed or irrigated). The משנה about onions and cowpeas fits רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, by the opinion the משנה follows, the tithing year can depend on how a plant was actually grown, not only on its species.

phrases.english: As we learned: seedless onions and cowpeas
from which one held back water
for thirty days before Rosh HaShana
are tithed for the past year
and are permitted in the Sabbatical year,
phrases.notes: He means when the new year starting is שביעית; they count as last year's crop.

phrases.english: and if not,
they are forbidden in the Sabbatical year
and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה behind רבי אבהו's answer in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That seedless onions and cowpeas are a real case where the two opinions differ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה ruling that these plants follow the old year if their water was held back for thirty days before ראש השנה, which fits רבי יוסי הגלילי's test.

steps.title: Why is the new year for trees on the first of שבט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the first of שבט is the new year for trees and asks for the reason behind that date.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: On the first of שבט is the new year for trees. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why this date was chosen. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about vegetables and grain. Now the focus shifts to trees. The question is simple: what makes the first of שבט the dividing point between one year's fruit and the next?

keyTerms.meaning: The new year for trees. Fruit is assigned to a year for tithes based on this date.
The Hebrew month that falls in midwinter.
A tree
What is the reason?

phrases.english: On the first of Shevat
is the new year for trees.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the vegetables discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה: the new year for trees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the new year for trees is set on the first of שבט.

steps.title: Most of the year's rain has already fallen
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, explains that by the first of שבט most of the year's rain has fallen, though most of the winter season is still ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: Because most of the year's rains have already fallen, and most of the season is still ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to the question of why the date is the first of שבט. The answer points to the rainfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first of שבט most of the rainy season's water has already come down. So the old year's rain is mostly finished, and new growth counts for the new year. The second half of his statement, 'most of the season is still ahead,' is unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
The year's rains
A season. Here it means the winter season.
Literally 'outside.' Here it means 'still to come.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said
Rabbi Oshaya said:
Since there have gone out
phrases.notes: 'Gone out' means the rains have already passed. They have fallen.

phrases.english: most of the year's rains,
and still most of the season is outside.
phrases.notes: He means most of the winter season is still ahead of us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By the first of שבט most of the year's rains have fallen, while most of the winter season is still ahead.

steps.title: What does he mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand רבי אושעיא's statement, since its second half seems not to fit as a reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by how the answer is worded and asks what it means. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Most of the rain has fallen' supports a new year starting now. 'Most of the season is still ahead' seems to argue against it. So how can both halves together be the reason?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? The גמרא asks this when someone's words are unclear.
And still

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the answer in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two halves of רבי אושעיא's reason fit together.

steps.title: Even though winter isn't over, most of the rain is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the statement should be read as 'even though': even though most of the winter is still ahead, most of the rain has fallen, and that is what counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Even though most of the season is still ahead, since most of the year's rains have already fallen, the new year starts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up the confusing wording. The second half is not a reason. It is an 'even though.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the rain, not the calendar season. Someone might think the year should wait until winter ends. The גמרא says no: once most of the rain is down, the old year's growing water is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It introduces a clearer reading of someone's words.
Even though
They have gone out, meaning they have passed

steps.whatToRemember: The new year for trees is the first of שבט because most of the year's rain has already fallen by then. This is true even though most of the winter season is still ahead.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹב תְּקוּפָה מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: even though most of the season is still outside,
since most of the year's rains have gone out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by rereading step 13 as an 'even though' statement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Read it as: even though most of the winter is still ahead, the new year starts because most of the rain has fallen.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's אתרוג picked on the first of שבט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי עקיבא picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and separated two tithes from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: It once happened that רבי עקיבא picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט, and he separated two tithes from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story from a ברייתא connected to the first of שבט. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא picked fruit exactly on the date that the משנה called the new year for trees. He took two tithes instead of one. This suggests he was unsure which year the אתרוג belonged to, so he covered both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
An incident, a story that actually happened
A citron fruit
He picked or gathered
He treated it a certain way, he acted with it
Tithes

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with Rabbi Akiva
who picked an etrog on the first of Shevat
and he treated it with two tithes,
phrases.notes: He was unsure which year it belonged to, so he took both מעשר שני and מעשר עני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא story connected to the first of שבט, the date just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא separated two tithes from an אתרוג he picked on the first of שבט.
